See also: pomáda

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French pommade.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [puˈma.ðə]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [poˈma.ðə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [poˈma.ða]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

pomada f (plural pomades)

  1. ointment, cream, pomade
  2. (Balearic, Menorca) gin with lemonade

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pomada”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “pomada”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026

Cebuano

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From English pomade, from French pommade (“ointment”), from Italian pomata, from pomo (“apple”), as such ointments were originally made from apples, + -ata (“(collective)”) (English -ade). Pomo is in turn from Latin pomum.

Noun

[edit]

pomada

  1. a pomade; a greasy or waxy substance that is used to style hair, making it look slick and shiny

Verb

[edit]

pomada

  1. to use pomade to style hair

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From French pommade, from Italian pomata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpomɑdɑ/, [ˈpo̞mɑ̝dɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -omɑdɑ
  • Syllabification(key): po‧ma‧da
  • Hyphenation(key): po‧ma‧da

Noun

[edit]

pomada

  1. pomade
    Synonym: hiusrasva
  2. sugar glaze (often colored pink)

pomada

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French pommade, from Italian pomata, from pomo (“apple”) +‎ -ata. By surface analysis, pomo +‎ -ada.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /puˈma.dɐ/, /poˈma.dɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /puˈma.dɐ/, /poˈma.dɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /poˈma.da/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /puˈma.dɐ/ [puˈma.ðɐ]

  • Hyphenation: po‧ma‧da

Noun

[edit]

pomada f (plural pomadas)

  1. ointment (cream with medicine)

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Kadiwéu: pomaada

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pomada”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “pomada” in Dicionário Aberto based on Novo Diccionário da Língua Portuguesa de Cândido de Figueiredo, 1913
  • “pomada”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “pomada”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

From poma +‎ -ada. Cognate with English pomade.

Pronunciation

  • Rhymes: -ada

Noun

[edit]

pomada f (plural pomadas)

  1. salve, ointment
    Synonym: ungüento
  2. cream
    Synonym: crema
